links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition: Chapter 8, Strings and Text Editing
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: string literals, indexes and slices, f-strings, string methods, code points, the clipboard projects and Pig Latin.

links.title: 3. An Informal Introduction to Python
links.why: The tutorial's first account of strings: quotes, escapes, raw strings, triple quotes, indexing, slicing and immutability.

links.title: 7. Input and Output
links.why: The tutorial section on fancier output formatting: f-strings, str.format() and the difference between str() and repr().

links.title: Built-in Types
links.why: Every string method with its exact rules, plus the sections on f-strings, t-strings and printf-style formatting.

links.title: 2. Lexical analysis
links.why: The language reference for string literals, prefixes, the full table of escape sequences and the grammar of f-strings and t-strings.

links.title: string — Common string operations
links.why: The format specification mini-language behind f-string specifiers, plus capwords and string.Template.

links.title: string.templatelib — Support for template string literals
links.why: The Template and Interpolation types that a t-string produces (Python 3.14).

links.title: Unicode HOWTO
links.why: Code points, encodings, UTF-8 and bytes versus text, explained for Python programmers.

links.title: codecs — Codec registry and base classes
links.why: The table of error handlers (strict, ignore, replace, backslashreplace and others) that encode() and decode() accept.

links.title: PEP 498 – Literal String Interpolation
links.why: The proposal that added f-strings in Python 3.6.

links.title: PEP 701 – Syntactic formalization of f-strings
links.why: Why Python 3.12 lifted the restrictions on quotes, backslashes and comments inside f-string fields.

links.title: PEP 750 – Template Strings
links.why: The proposal behind t-strings in Python 3.14 and the reasons for a Template object instead of a str.

links.title: PEP 686 – Make UTF-8 mode default
links.why: Why open() without an encoding is locale-dependent today and the plan to make UTF-8 the default in Python 3.15.

links.title: Pragmatic Unicode (Ned Batchelder)
links.why: The talk that the chapter recommends on Unicode. It was opened and its title read; none of the chapter's findings rests on it.

links.title: Python Tutor
links.why: A site for stepping through Python programs; it was opened and its title read, and is offered for trying the chapter's string programs line by line.

_note: Every url was opened with a page fetch (HTTP 200) and its title read on the date in 'checked'. The Python documentation pages served on that date were headed Python 3.14.8, while the chapter research read the 3.14.4 sources. The textbook chapter's page title as served is 'Chapter 8 - Strings and Text Editing, Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd Ed'. The talk and Python Tutor pages were opened and their titles read but not studied. No video or discussion thread is listed: none was opened and read, so the course owner may add checked ones here.
